question: Should NonfinitePositionPolicy::RejectLeaf become the default nonfinite-position policy?
change_under_test: Tuning::default().nonfinite_position(NonfinitePositionPolicy::RejectLeaf) versus Tuning::default() (shipped Abort); everything else the shipped sampler default (Metric::diagonal, Adaptation::default, Init::uniform at its shipped radius via uniform_starts, Limits::admit_worst_case), 4 chains x 1000/1000, 4 threads
arm_order_within_pair: abort then reject_leaf, back to back, same seed

gates.note: on every posteriordb reference parameter; plus finite draws; a cell that did not complete fails every gate

statistic: geomean over the 17 house models of the per-model seed-median min bulk ESS per gradient (total target calls incl. warmup), ratio reject_leaf / abort

wp50_assets.source: C:/dev/owalnuts-wt/windows-native-root-cause/STUDIES/bridgestan_windows_root_cause_v3/build/static/ (the WP50D/E static-runtime build, hashes as in bridgestan_windows_root_cause_v5/protocol.json)

funnel.gate: |MCSE z| <= 2 for P(omega < -5) on every seed

predictions.P1: reject_leaf completes every run abort completes, plus every stress case abort loses
predictions.P2: draws (and per-chain target calls) bit-identical on every cell where abort completed
predictions.P3: reject_leaf passes >= as many stress-set gate cells as abort
predictions.P4: on every rescued cell (abort did not complete, reject_leaf did) max |z| <= 3
predictions.P5: every rescued run shows >= 1 retained divergence
predictions.P6: funnel |z| <= 2 on every seed under both arms

flip_iff: D1: bit-identical on 100% of completed-abort cells (all blocks incl. funnel)
D2: reject_leaf completes strictly more runs than abort, counted over the whole manifest
D3: no rescued posterior run has max |z| > 4 on a reference parameter while passing all other gates
D4: the funnel check (|z| <= 2 every seed) passes under reject_leaf
decision_rule.if_flip: make RejectLeaf the default in walnutpie::KernelTuning and sampler::Tuning; tests/kernel_fingerprint.rs changes only if a fingerprint changes; CHANGELOG entry naming this study; cargo test
decision_rule.if_not: document why; Abort stays the default

rules: cells strictly sequential in manifest order, one at a time, 4 threads; no cell rerun or tuned after results; a timeout, error or abort is a recorded result; amendments only for cells not yet run and committed before them
